page_title: SRE error budgets and maintenance windows | Google Cloud Blog

sources.entry: How maintenance windows affect your error budget

summary.name: SRE error budgets and maintenance windows
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud blog article explaining how planned maintenance windows should count (or not count) against an SRE error budget, with scenarios and strategies.
use_cases: deciding whether scheduled downtime should count against an SLO
planning maintenance windows for a low-traffic period
calculating remaining error budget after an outage
designing multi-region services to avoid maintenance downtime
summary.what_it_does: The article walks through how maintenance windows interact with error budgets, defined as the allowed error remainder under an SLO. It covers scenarios such as trading-hours services, localized services with daily traffic valleys, and global services with flat traffic. It describes two approaches for localized services: traffic projection using past data and a captive portal, and treating maintenance time as downtime against the budget, with a worked example of a 99% SLO over 28 days. It also discusses edge cases like emergency "silver bullet" exceptions and argues that maintenance windows should only be excluded from the budget if they are accepted as a fixed risk with clear communication and rollback plans.
notable: Worked example: a 99% availability SLO over 28 days allows about 7 hours 20 minutes of downtime, so a 2-hour window uses 27% of the budget
Argues that excluding maintenance from the error budget implicitly accepts recurring burn with no plan to eliminate windows
Recommends multi-region designs that disconnect regions for maintenance instead of scheduled global downtime
caveats: Opinion and guidance article, not a software tool; it describes practices rather than a product
Recommendations depend on business agreements and traffic patterns, and the article says no single approach fits all services
